en: Saraṇaduka, Hetusahetukadukādi (The Pair on Having a Refuge, the Pair on Being with Cause and Having Causes, etc.)
Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*anāsava*), neither-root, and rootless, there arises a state that is non-conflict, both-root and with-root, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is non-conflict, neither-root, and rootless, there arises a state that is conflict (*sāsava*), both-root and with-root, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Two [answers] for root... pe ... for resultant.
One [condition]... [and so on] ... two non-disappearance conditions.

Dependent on a state that is neither-with-conflict (na-araṇa), neither-rootless (na-ahetuka), and not-root (nanahetu), there arises a state that is without-conflict (araṇa), with-root (sahetuka), and not-root (na-hetu) by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya). Dependent on a state that is neither-with-conflict, neither-rootless, and not-root...
A state that has a root-cause and is itself not a root-cause arises by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root [condition] there are two; ...
under the resultant [condition] there is one; ... under the non-disappearance [condition] there are two.
